questions.question: Which decimal is equal to 3/4?
questions.explain: To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the top by the bottom: 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75. The common trap is just writing the two digits you see (0.34 or 0.43) instead of dividing.

questions.question: Which fraction becomes a repeating decimal when you divide?
questions.explain: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.333… , which never ends, so it is a repeating decimal; 1/4 = 0.25, 1/5 = 0.2 and 1/8 = 0.125 all stop, so they are terminating. The trap is assuming a bigger denominator always repeats — it is the division that decides.

questions.question: In Ms. Chan's class, 3 out of every 5 students walk to school. Written as a percent, that is:
questions.explain: Percent means "out of 100", so scale 3/5 up: 3/5 = 6/10 = 60/100 = 60%. The trap is reading the digits straight across (35%) or multiplying 3 × 5 = 15%.

questions.question: Which fraction is equal to 45%?
questions.explain: Percent means out of 100, so 45% = 45/100, and dividing top and bottom by 5 gives 9/20. The trap is misplacing the place value and writing 45/10, which is 450%.

questions.question: At a shoreline cleanup in Stanley Park, Maya's group collected 80 pieces of litter, and 28 of them were plastic straws. What percent of the litter was plastic straws?
questions.explain: Write the part over the whole and convert: 28/80 = 0.35 = 35%. The trap is using the count 28 as the percent — that would only work if the total were 100.

questions.question: Four amounts are marked on a number line: 0.6, 5/8, 65%, and 0.7. Which list puts them in order from least to greatest?
questions.explain: Change everything to decimals first: 0.6, 5/8 = 0.625, 65% = 0.65, 0.7 — so the order is 0.6, 5/8, 65%, 0.7. The trap is comparing different forms without converting, or assuming a fraction like 5/8 must be smallest because its digits look small.

questions.question: Of the 8 bags of litter Dev's team collected at the beach, 7 held recyclable material. Written as a decimal, what is 7/8, and what kind of decimal is it?
questions.explain: Divide top by bottom: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, which ends, so it is a terminating decimal. The trap is dividing the wrong way (8 ÷ 7 = 1.142…) — always divide the numerator by the denominator.

questions.question: Kai's class is tracking how close each group is to filling half its recycling bin. Which group's amount is closest to the benchmark 1/2?
questions.explain: Turn each into a decimal and compare to 0.5: 0.45 is 0.05 away, 2/5 = 0.4 is 0.1 away, 48% = 0.48 is only 0.02 away, and 5/9 = 0.555… is about 0.055 away, so 48% is closest. The trap is comparing mixed forms by eye instead of converting them all to the same form first.

questions.question: Four students weighed the plastic they collected at a shoreline cleanup: Ava 0.7 kg, Ben 0.65 kg, Cara 3/4 kg, Dev 0.68 kg. Who collected the most plastic?
questions.explain: Write them all the same way: Cara's 3/4 kg = 0.75 kg, which beats 0.7, 0.68 and 0.65. The trap is thinking 0.65 or 0.68 is bigger than 0.7 because they have more digits — line up the tenths place first, where 7 beats 6.

questions.question: At Riverside School, 12 of the 40 Grade 7 students joined the shoreline cleanup. In Grade 6, 26% of the students joined. Which grade had the greater percent join, and by how much?
questions.explain: Convert the Grade 7 ratio to a percent first: 12/40 = 0.30 = 30%, and 30% − 26% = 4%, so Grade 7 was greater by 4%. The trap is treating the count 12 as "12%" — a number of students only becomes a percent after you compare it to the total.

questions.question: Noah divides 2 ÷ 3 and his calculator shows 0.6666667. He writes 0.67 on his poster. Which statement is true?
options: 0.67 is the exact value, because 2/3 is a terminating decimal.
0.666… is the rounded value and 0.67 is the exact one.
2/3 is a repeating decimal, 0.666…, so 0.67 is only a rounded value and is slightly greater than 2/3.
2/3 is a repeating decimal, 0.666…, so 0.67 is only a rounded value and is slightly less than 2/3.
questions.explain: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666… repeats forever, so 0.67 is a rounded value; since 0.67 > 0.666…, it is slightly greater than 2/3. The trap is believing the calculator's cut-off display is exact — a repeating decimal never ends, so only the fraction 2/3 is exact.

questions.question: At a beach cleanup, the ratio of cans to bottles collected was 3 : 2, and there were 120 cans and bottles altogether. What percent of these 120 items were bottles?
questions.explain: A ratio of 3 : 2 means 5 equal parts in total, so bottles are 2/5 of the items, and 2/5 = 0.4 = 40% (that is 48 bottles out of 120). The trap is writing 2/3 and getting about 67% — a percent compares the part to the whole, not one part to the other part.
